verification: All reference logit replays pass atol 2e-5 / rtol 1e-5 and exactly reproduce binary necessity/sufficiency outcomes. Independently checked source hashes, finite logits, unique support counts, effective budgets and binary metric arithmetic in all 1200 rows.
finding: The two support-search variants have higher mean binary necessity and sufficiency than this fixed-config GNNExplainer baseline at all three budgets. Ungrouped and coarse-union searches still have identical binary outcomes, so this does not establish an independent coarsening contribution. Favorable aggregate means do not imply per-query dominance.
baseline_scope: Existing PyG GNNExplainer, 100 epochs and lr 0.01 with package defaults, fixed node features, frozen predictor and native directed message gates. Gates multiply GCN messages after normalization; they are not tied undirected renormalized adjacency gates. All methods' discrete supports use the same original-graph intervention protocol. This training/evaluation distinction is disclosed, not silently changed to our objective.
limitations: One dataset/checkpoint, one hashed initialization per query, previously inspected validation queries, default rather than tuned baseline settings, no test-set or statistical-significance claim. Equal support sizes do not mean equal optimization cost. Historical search times are not paired runtime measurements against this new baseline run.
next_work: Broaden joint-objective baseline comparison and validate configurations separately before final method selection. Do not treat the original-edge search improvement over one baseline as evidence for the paper's global coarsening claim.
manuscript: Only the baseline masking/normalization distinction is clarified. Empirical LaTeX numbers, tables and figures remain unchanged.
